biography: Juliano Moro's journey began on the sun-baked karting tracks of São Paulo, a far cry from the glitz of international motorsport. His father, a mechanic, instilled in him a deep understanding of machinery and a fierce competitive spirit. A defining moment came at age 16 when, despite starting last after a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to victory, showcasing his relentless determination. This win caught the attention of JLM Racing, who brought him into their development program. Moro's ascent was steady, marked by consistent performances and a tenacious defensive style. Now, at 29, he's at the peak of his abilities, a seasoned competitor known for his unwavering focus and ability to extract the maximum from his car. While lacking the outright flamboyance of some, his reliability makes him a formidable opponent, and JLM Racing considers him their cornerstone driver.
drivingStyle: Moro's driving is characterized by calculated precision and defensive prowess. He rarely over-drives the car, instead focusing on maintaining consistent lap times and exploiting any mistakes from his rivals. He's a master of tire management, often able to run longer stints than his competitors. In wheel-to-wheel combat, he's notoriously difficult to overtake, using his car's width to defend his position and force his rivals into unfavorable lines. He thrives under pressure, rarely cracking even in the most intense situations, making him a formidable force in the closing stages of a race.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Vargas
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, fueled by contrasting personalities and aggressive on-track battles.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A strategic rivalry, as Dubois is known to aggressively use her qualifying position and pit strategy to her advantage, often placing her directly in Moro's path.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A clash of driving philosophies, with Tanaka's aggressive overtaking style often leading to contact with Moro's more conservative approach.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of socks for every race weekend, believing they bring him good luck.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Refuses to walk under any ladders, no matter how inconvenient it might be.
famousQuote: "It's not about being the fastest for one lap, it's about being the fastest for every lap."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in 2022, his home race, after a strategic masterclass and flawless defensive driving in the final laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2021 season due to a mechanical failure, costing him the championship by a single point.
